story-01-start-here.label: Start here
lines: Ancient philosophy for young men who want a life that means something.
Purpose. Meaning in suffering. Amor fati. Being a good man. Seeing the beauty in this life.
“It is impossible for a man to learn what he thinks he already knows.”
story-01-start-here.footer: Three posts a day. Turn on notifications.

story-02-purpose-plato.label: Purpose
lines: “The unexamined life is not worth living.”
Socrates said this at his own trial, choosing death over a life without questions.
Ask yourself today: what am I actually living for?

story-03-suffering-epictetus.label: Suffering
lines: “It is difficulties that show what men are.”
Epictetus was born a slave and walked with a limp. He didn’t ask for an easier life. He asked to be equal to the one he had.
story-03-suffering-epictetus.footer: Screenshot this for your next hard day.

story-04-virtue-aristotle.label: Virtue
lines: “We become just by doing just acts, temperate by doing temperate acts, brave by doing brave acts.”
You don’t find your character. You build it, one choice at a time.

story-05-amorfati-epictetus.label: Amor fati
lines: “Do not seek to have events happen as you want them to, but instead want them to happen as they do happen, and your life will go well.”
Not giving up. Saying yes to the life in front of you.

story-06-purpose-aristotle.label: Purpose
lines: Aristotle asked what a good life is for. His answer:
“The human good turns out to be activity of soul in accordance with virtue.”
Happiness isn’t a feeling you wait for. It’s the way you live.

story-07-suffering-frankl.label: Suffering
lines: “In some ways suffering ceases to be suffering at the moment it finds a meaning.”
Viktor Frankl, Man’s Search for Meaning
He wrote it after surviving Auschwitz. Your pain can become your purpose.

story-08-virtue-plato.label: Virtue
lines: “The victory over self is of all victories the first and best.”
Before you try to win anything out there, win the fight in here.

story-09-beauty-marcus.label: Beauty
lines: “Dwell on the beauty of life. Watch the stars, and see yourself running with them.”
Go outside tonight. Look up for one full minute.

story-10-amorfati-nietzsche.label: Amor fati
lines: “My formula for greatness in a human being is amor fati: that one wants nothing to be different, not forward, not backward, not in all eternity.”
Love your fate. Even the parts that hurt made you.

story-11-suffering-seneca.label: Suffering
lines: The hard week ahead isn’t in your way. It’s your chance.

carousel-1.label: For young men
lines: 5 ancient one-liners for young men who want a life that matters.
“No man is free who is not master of himself.”
Freedom starts with your habits, not your circumstances.
“When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.”
Pick a direction. Then the storms start working for you.
“One swallow does not make a summer, nor does one day.”
One good day isn’t a good life. Keep showing up.
“Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.”
“How long will you wait before you demand the best of yourself?”

lines: Which one are you living by this week?
